_meta.note: Independent recomputation of the pipeline outputs from the raw NASA PSI tables and the rules written in pipeline/spec/*.json and pipeline/README.md. check.py does not import the pipeline code. A check that fails names a disagreement; it does not say which side is right.

checks.verifies: Every value with a real source column is found in its raw NASA cell and is explained by a rule that the spec states (exact copy, declared factor, number in the cell text, spec vocabulary), or is one of the exceptions README declares, exactly as declared and with its flag on the test.

class_meaning.exact: same text (ignoring case) or the same number as the raw cell
class_meaning.declared_factor: a number in the cell times the factor or unit conversion declared in sources.json
class_meaning.number_in_text: the only number written in a longer cell
class_meaning.vocabulary: the spec maps the cell text to this category (sources.json 'map', or the keywords listed in the variable's meaning in variables.json)
class_meaning.one_of_several_numbers: one of several numbers written in the cell; which one is chosen is an engine rule that the spec does not state
class_meaning.unit_in_cell: a number in the cell converted from the unit written next to it to the variable's unit
class_meaning.text_in_cell: the value is written inside a longer cell
class_meaning.material_alias_in_cell: the cell names a material of materials.json (id or alias) and the value is another alias of the same material
class_meaning.declared_exception_flagged: a value of a kind README declares in the table 'Values that are not literally in a NASA cell' (one of two oxygen numbers written, named by a publication; material from the BASS-II ReadMe; cell of the row above): it is exactly what the declared rule gives and the test carries the named flag
class_meaning.unexplained: no rule found that leads from the raw cell to the value
class_meaning.empty_cell: the raw cell is empty but a value is recorded. This includes columns that sources.json lists under 'fill_down' (the value is the cell of a row above): the rule that an empty cell means 'not recorded' and is never filled in does not allow it
class_meaning.category_not_in_cell: a text value that is not written in the cell and that no spec file maps the cell text to (the mapping lives in engine code, not in the spec)
class_meaning.computed_midpoint: the value is the midpoint of two numbers in the cell: computed, not copied, and not a formula of variables.json
class_meaning.reference_label_number: the number is the label of a note or figure in the cell ('Note 4', 'Fig. 5'), not a measurement
class_meaning.assumed_unit: the value needs a unit conversion whose unit is neither written in the cell nor declared in sources.json
class_meaning.declared_factor_not_applied: sources.json declares a factor for the column but the value equals the raw number without it
class_meaning.unit_ignored: the number is copied although the unit written after it in the cell is not the unit of the variable
class_meaning.declared_exception_without_flag: a value of a kind that README declares (one of two oxygen numbers named by a publication, material from the BASS-II ReadMe, cell of the row above) but the test does not carry the flag README names for it
class_meaning.spec_rule_gives_other_value: the rule written in the spec for this column (sources.json '_meta.sample_keywords' or '_meta.documented_start') leads from the cell to a different value, or to none
class_meaning.two_number_cell_not_documented: an oxygen value from a cell with two numbers whose exact text is not listed under 'documented_start' (sources.json): such a cell gives no value

declared_exception_flagged.note: material_from_readme; sample_keywords thickness rule (0.1 mm); flag fuel_material:not_written_in_cell_named_in_readme present
material_from_readme; sample_keywords thickness rule (0.2 mm); flag fuel_material:not_written_in_cell_named_in_readme present
material_from_readme; sample_keywords thickness rule (0.4 mm); flag fuel_material:not_written_in_cell_named_in_readme present
material_from_readme; sample_keywords thickness rule (0.3 mm); flag fuel_material:not_written_in_cell_named_in_readme present
material_from_readme; sample_keywords thickness rule (0.4 mm); flag fuel_material:not_written_in_cell_named_in_readme present

declared_factor.column: O initial ambient composition; mole fraction
CO initial ambient composition; mole fraction

numbers_written_with_a_leading_zero.note: Copied as written (for example '037 mm' read as 37). Not a failure of the trace; a human should look at the NASA page, because the source cell may be a typing error.

checks.verifies: Every test names an existing raw file and a row inside it, and no two tests share a raw row.
Every non-empty variable cell of tests.csv has exactly one row in values_long.csv with the same value, unit, file and row, and every values_long row has its cell in tests.csv.

In every test-level table, each raw row that sources.json keeps (all 'require' columns filled, no 'exclude' rule, not a cell-for-cell repeat of an earlier row) is exactly one test, no other row is a test, and the test id is the 'test_id' template filled from that row.

details.note: A test whose id cell is empty in the raw table is listed here for a human to look at; it is not counted as a failure because no spec rule excludes such a row. Test ids are compared after removing whitespace inside the raw id cell; the spec does not state that step.

checks.verifies: A non-empty raw cell of a mapped column that left its variable empty carries a flag '<variable>:<reason>' (README: a cell that a rule cannot read stays empty and gets a flag).

details.note: Cells that hold no letter or digit (a dash) or only 'n/a' are counted apart and do not fail the check: they say that there is no value. The pipeline is not consistent here: the same kind of cell gets a flag in some tables and none in others.

checks.verifies: In a column mapped to both flow_cms and flow_min_cms, flow_cms is the number the cell starts with and flow_min_cms the lowest number written, and flow_min_cms is empty where the cell holds potentiometer settings or bracketed numbers (the meanings in variables.json), unless a flag on the variable says otherwise.

meanings_applied.flow_cms: Imposed flow speed at the start of the test (the number the flow cell starts with)
meanings_applied.flow_min_cms: Lowest flow speed written in the cell that lists the settings of the test. Not read where the cell also holds fan potentiometer settings or anything in brackets, or where the cell does not start with a flow speed

details.note: How the engine chooses among the numbers of a cell is written in pipeline/rules.py, which this check does not read. It applies the two meanings literally.

checks.verifies: For every test of a column read with rule 'sample_keywords', fuel_material, sample_geometry and rod_diameter_mm in tests.csv are what the entries of sources.json give for the cell (also where they give no value), and the flag 'not_written_in_cell_named_in_readme' is on exactly the tests whose material is not written in the cell.

An oxygen cell with two numbers gives a value only if 'documented_start' lists its exact text: then o2_pct is the listed number, which is one of the two written, and the test carries the flag 'range_in_source_start_value_named_in_publication'; otherwise o2_pct is empty with the flag 'range_in_source_start_value_not_documented'. o2_range_as_written holds the cell text in both cases.
Values marked '(constant in sources.json)' equal the constant declared for the test's source, and every declared constant is recorded for every test of the source.

Every derived value equals its formula in variables.json recomputed from the test's own recorded inputs (tolerance 1e-4), is absent exactly when an input is empty or a skip_if holds, and carries the flags the spec names.
material_id is the materials.json entry whose aliases contain fuel_material (ignoring case and surrounding spaces); a name that is not listed has no id and the flag material_id:not_in_vocabulary.
No value in tests.csv lies outside the 'ranges' of variables.json.

A raw reading for which a 'consistency' expression of variables.json holds (for example a final oxygen below 5, or above the initial oxygen + 0.5) has no value in tests.csv and carries '<variable>:<flag>'; no other reading of the variable was emptied by the rule or carries its flag.

need_tests.csv lists exactly the in-scope tests that record every required condition (or have it documented for their table) and at least one outcome of each need, with objective_link 'stated' only when a 'stated_by' link of the investigation has verdict 'supported'.

capability_matrix.csv has one row per need and source whose counts (tests in scope, with required conditions, with an outcome, usable), status, missing and documented conditions, objective_link and publication quote equal the recomputation from tests.csv, needs.json and sources.json.

Every 'stated_by' link of needs.json has a known verdict; its record sentence, where given, is literally in the named field of the PSI record; its publication, where given, is a reference item with a quote; and a link with verdict 'supported' has a publication.
objective_links.csv lists exactly the links of needs.json 'stated_by' (all verdicts) with record field and sentence, publication item, the quote of that item in references.json, and verdict.

Every 'see_also' entry of scenarios.json and every 'documented_elsewhere' entry of sources.json is literally in the named PSI record field, raw table cell or references.json item, and a variable documented elsewhere has no value in the tests of that table.
Every count of coverage_grid.csv equals the number of tests that tests.csv puts in that fuel phase, oxygen basis, oxygen bin and pressure bin (coverage.json), and no non-empty cell is missing.
The counts of coverage_grid.csv add up to the number of tests.
For every scenario and test, the oxygen, pressure, flow and gravity marks and the tier of scenario_tests.csv equal the recomputation from tests.csv and the ranges of scenarios.json.
Every numeric column and investigation list of scenario_needs.csv equals the recomputation from tests.csv, the recomputed usable tests and the recomputed tiers.
The status of every scenario and need follows the status_rule of scenarios.json.
The oxygen, pressure, gravity and no-usable-test gap codes of scenario_needs.csv say which variable has no usable test in range or is not in the table (README 'Scenarios').

A scenario that sets a flow range carries a flow gap code exactly when no usable test has its flow in range (README: gap codes say which variable - oxygen, pressure, flow, gravity - has no usable test in range or is not in the table).

The added_gas mark of scenario_tests.csv is 'none' only where carbon dioxide and helium are both recorded as 0, 'co2_or_helium' where either is above 0, and 'not_recorded' otherwise (scenarios.json 'added_gas').
Every row of indicators.csv (value, n_tests, investigations, texts) equals the recomputation of its template over its population, filter and grouping (indicators.json), and no row is missing.
indicator_tests.csv lists exactly the tests behind each indicator row, with the value each test contributes.
Every reference item id used in needs.json, indicators.json and scenarios.json exists in references.json.
need_references.csv has exactly the reference items each need lists, with the text, place, document and URL of references.json.

index.json lists the scenarios of scenarios.json and then every oxygen bin x pressure bin of coverage.json, every package file exists and has the contract's shape: environment with ranges and basis, and one block per need of needs.json with all its fields.

status, counts and gap codes of every need block equal the environment's row in scenario_needs.csv or atmosphere_cells.csv; index.json carries the same status, the first statement of the block as status text, and the caveat of the scenario.
atmosphere_cells.csv equals the recomputation of every oxygen bin x pressure bin of coverage.json as a scenario whose ranges are the bin edges, with no flow range and no gravity level.

matched_tests of every need block is exactly the usable tests of tier atmosphere, oxygen_only or pressure_only; marks, flags, source file and row equal tests.csv; every value, unit and source column equals values_long.csv and covers the need's recorded variables.

objective entries equal the links of needs.json, the investigations list equals the usable tests per investigation and tier with the title of the PSI record, references equal the need's items in references.json, and every gap code has a sentence.
usable_elsewhere of every need block (tests of tier other: how many, lowest and highest recorded ambient oxygen and pressure, investigations) equals the recomputation from tests.csv.
The indicators of every need block equal the need's indicators recomputed over the tests of their population whose tier in this environment is atmosphere, oxygen_only or pressure_only.

Every number written in a statement of an evidence package is a field of the same need block (for an indicator sentence: of its indicator entry; for an environment sentence: of its recorded_tests row), or one of the two sums that statements.json declares.

details.note: statements.json declares two computed fields: the number of entries of matched_tests and counts.atmosphere + counts.oxygen_only. A number found only there is counted apart; it is recomputed here from the block.

checks.verifies: No statement of an evidence package contains the words safe, unsafe, flammable, sufficient, representative, proves or confirms (outside a need name or an indicator reading copied from the spec, and outside a sentence quoted word for word from a NASA record or a publication).

environment.recorded_tests of every package lists, per investigation and fuel phase, how many tests of tests.csv (whatever the need) have tier atmosphere, oxygen_only or pressure_only in that environment, and 'counted_for' names the needs that count at least one of these matched tests.

matched_ranges of every need block (how many matched tests record oxygen of the surrounding atmosphere and pressure, with the lowest and highest recorded value) equals the recomputation from tests.csv over the counted tests of tier atmosphere, oxygen_only or pressure_only.
investigation_facts.json has one entry per PSI record (numeric order) with title, acronym, DOI and license of the record, its tables as in sources.json, and test counts that add up to tests.csv.
For every investigation and every table, the listed variables are exactly those with a value, and each n, min, max and value count equals the recomputation from tests.csv.
stated_needs of every investigation equal the links of needs.json, and capability equals the rows of capability_matrix.csv (status, counts, objective_link per need and table).

Every number written in a statement of investigation_facts.json is a field of the same entry (of the table or need the sentence is about), and no statement contains a word that judges safety or sufficiency.
Every raw table named in data/psi/manifest.json and in sources.json exists, and its size (and hash, when the manifest carries one) matches the manifest.

details.note: The manifest carries sizes only; contents are compared by size, not by hash.

checks.verifies: Every entry of spec/findings.json points to an item of references.json; findings.csv has one row per entry, and its text, quote, where, title, version, access, url and reference id are those of the item and its document, its kind, needs and condition columns those of the entry; the 'findings' of findings_by_environment.json carry the same text, quote, place and document.

Every normalized number of an entry (oxygen, pressure, flow; each end of a range) follows from its condition_basis: literally present in the basis words or values, or, for a pressure, a number of the basis times the factor of its unit (1 psi = 6.894757 kPa, 1 atm = 101.325 kPa), rounded to 3 decimals. The basis words are in the item's text or quote, a values key exists, and a gravity level or fuel phase has a word of its vocabulary behind it.

details.note: A vocabulary word is accepted where it starts a word of the basis ('solid' in 'thick solids'); the rule text does not say whole word. Such cases: BASS13.nitrogen:solid

checks.verifies: For each scenario and each need (and 'general'), the three lists of findings_by_environment.json, the entries counted under other_conditions and moved_for_gravity, the counts, and for each listed entry the relations of matched_on, not_stated and flow are recomputed from findings.csv and scenarios.json by the rule of spec/findings.json _meta.lists.

Every number in a fixed sentence of findings_by_environment.json is one of the counts of its block (n_at, n_about, n_general, n_listed, n_not_full_text), and no sentence or sentence template holds a word of spec/findings.json forbidden_words.

answers/ holds one file per scenario of scenarios.json and need of needs.json (36) and index.json, and nothing else; index.json lists them in spec order with the file's top line and the number of entries of every list it names.

Rung 1 of every answer file: status, counts and the gap codes of rung 4 equal the scenario's row of scenario_needs.csv; matched is the number of matched tests of the evidence package block; matched ranges, fuel phases, investigations, documented sentences and indicator values are those of the block; the copied sentences are the block's statements selected by answers.json rung1.copied_statements, in order and unchanged, and the gap sentences are the block's gap texts.

Rung 2 of every answer file: the scenario's cells, the candidate cells and the listed cells are recomputed from coverage.json, scenarios.json and atmosphere_cells.csv by answers.json 'near'; every listed cell carries the counts and status of its row, matched and also_matched_at_the_condition recomputed from the evidence packages, the environment's range words, and the counts of the rung.

details.note: answers.json defines no rule for n_cells_with_repeating_tier; it is compared with the number of listed cells whose row has a test of tier oxygen_only or pressure_only and is reported, not failed.

checks.verifies: Every finding that findings_by_environment.json lists for the scenario under the need or under 'general' is in the answer file exactly once, placed by its kind (answers.json placement: criterion -> frame.criteria; gap -> frame.nasa_questions or rung4.stated_open_elsewhere; result, caveat -> the rung 3 list of its list), with applies, the name of its list, text and quote equal to references.json, the place and document of findings.csv, the order of placement.order, and the counts of frame, rung 3 and rung 4 recomputed from the lists.

The top line of every answer file starts with the fixed start of answers.json and is the one its rule selects: the first 'tests' sentence and the first 'published' sentence whose conditions hold for the fields recomputed from rungs 1 to 3, filled with those fields; id and fields as the rule says.

Every number in every sentence of an answer file is found in the block the sentence belongs to (top line: its fields; frame, rung 2, 3 and 4 sentences: the counts of the rung; a cell sentence: its cell; a copied package sentence: the copied package block of rung 1; a search sentence: the search entry), and the file's 'sentences' are exactly the sentences of its blocks.

No template of spec/answers.json holds a digit or a word of its forbidden_words, and no sentence of an answer file holds such a word (whole words; outside the need name, a reading copied from the spec and a sentence quoted word for word from a NASA record or a publication, which are counted apart).

raw_inventory.json has one entry per PSI record (numeric order); files and bytes per investigation, per PSI category and per kind (with extensions and archive content), the listing rows and repeats, the largest file of each kind, the totals, and the id patterns of the file names are recounted from the saved listings by the rules of raw_kinds.json, each file id counted once.

details.note: raw_kinds.json does not define 'distinct_ids'; it is compared with the number of distinct strings the pattern matches in the searched names and reported, not failed. Kinds are read from the name without prefix and extension (name_rule); id patterns from the whole name.

checks.verifies: Every number in the sentence of a raw_inventory.json entry is a field of the same entry, and every size written in it (GB from 10^9 bytes, MB below, one decimal) is a byte count of the entry in that unit.

gap_states.csv recounted from tests.csv: one row per investigation x need variable and state; n of N and the split of a mixed row as the README states it; the state of the other tests follows the fixed order (entry in raw_columns.json, then documented_elsewhere of sources.json, then not_in_sampled_files); file groups, files and bytes are those of the spec.

need_gap_states.csv: for every scenario, need and required or outcome variable, the in-scope and counted tests equal capability_matrix.csv (tests, and usable_tests of the stated rows) and need_tests.csv; the states of the tests and the counted tests left unmatched because the variable is empty are recounted from tests.csv and scenario_tests.csv; the counted tests per need are the frozen numbers.

retrieval_queue.csv: one row per investigation, variable and file group for the variables in state column (one row per group with an entry) or not_in_sampled_files (one row per unopened group of the spec), only where a test of an investigation linked as supported to a need that uses the variable lacks the value; the numbers are recounted; retrievable_by_reading is yes only where an entry of the group is a sensor series or a value per test in a results file, carries no code of differs_from_definition and has link_kind literal_key_or_label; the rows are sorted by the stated rule and ranked 1..n.

raw_values.csv: every row names a PSI file id of the listing of its investigation with the listed name and bytes; a test_id is given only with literal link evidence and exists in tests.csv for the same investigation; a series row has n_readings >= 1, min <= first, last <= max as stored numbers, and the rows of the lowest and the highest reading inside its first and last row.

spec/raw_columns.json: every group with a name_regex has the files and bytes that the regex gives on the saved listing (less exclude_ids); every sample and entry file id is in the listing with the listed name and bytes; every entry carries the name pattern, files and bytes of its group, a standard variable of a need, a column_is and header_kind of _meta, has_values true, a link_to_table_row, a link_kind of _meta and a list of codes of _meta.differs_from_definition.
tests.csv, need_tests.csv, scenario_needs.csv and scenario_tests.csv have the sha256 of the snapshot of 2026-11-14 17:30 KST that the README names.

raw_values_effect.json: the Saffire lowest and highest readings times the psi factor of spec/findings.json, their pressure bins and scenario ranges, and the SAME-R counts per size statistic are recounted from raw_values.csv, tests.csv and the specs; the file states that nothing is adopted.

Every need block of every evidence package has raw_state for each required variable: the counted and in-scope test numbers equal need_tests.csv and the need's scope, and the tests per state (summed over investigations) equal this check's recount; every gap entry has raw_state for its variable.

raw_file_groups.csv: the files and bytes of the groups add up, per investigation and kind, to the files and bytes of raw_inventory.json; in every group the files and bytes by link level add up to the group.

test_files.csv: every test_id is a test of tests.csv of the same investigation and is the test of its table row (source_file, source_row); every table_row_key names a row of an experimental table of the investigation; levels are test or day_or_session.

Every listed file is tied again by the ordered rules of spec/raw_names.json with this check's own code; the files and bytes by link level per investigation, per group of raw_file_groups.csv and per row of test_files.csv equal the outputs; the suffix codes too. SKIP without the git-ignored listings.

raw_layers_summary.json: per investigation and overall, the names layer equals the sums of raw_file_groups.csv, the structure layer the sample files of spec/raw_columns.json, the values layer the files of raw_values.csv, the archive layer archive_members_sample.csv; the overall numbers are the sums; the fixed sentences carry these numbers.

The columns that the name layer added to gap_states.csv, retrieval_queue.csv and need_gap_states.csv (videos and archives tied by name to the tests that lack the value, the class of on-screen text) and the fields added to the raw_state items of the evidence packages are recounted from test_files.csv, tests.csv and spec/raw_names.json; no sentence says that the quantity of an item can be read from a video.

spec/raw_names.json: every investigation of the listings is present; every meaning is a quote of 25 words or fewer with document, PSI file id and place, and the file id is a file of a listing of the same investigation (SKIP for the ids without listings); every rule names columns of its tables and known transforms.

question_chain.csv: the placement of every test (scenario_tests.csv oxygen and pressure match, recomputed); the quantity rows of each scenario, need, role and variable sum to the tests in the need's scope and to its counted tests, per placement; fixtures of design.md section 10 (lunar habitat 26 / 676 / 63 / 1,059; solid 0 / 237 / 139; ISS 179 / 739 / 106 / 800; Mars habitat no range set for 1,824).

question_chain.csv: the location of every quantity of every test recomputed from tests.csv, raw_values.csv, spec/raw_columns.json and spec/sources.json (table cell, value read, column seen, document sentence, not found), aggregated by scenario, need, role, variable, investigation, placement and location; summed over placement the rows equal need_gap_states.csv (required and outcome roles); lunar habitat P1 pressure: raw column 134, document only 129, not found 113.

Counted tests placed inside equal tests_atmosphere of scenario_needs.csv; question_chain_counts.csv per scenario, need, placement and pair: tests in scope, counted, not counted split into objective not stated, no outcome in the table, a required condition missing (recomputed); claims.md: of the 9 CFI-G tests inside the lunar ranges 7 are not stated and 2 hold no outcome for S1; the 17 counted lunar S1 tests are FLEX.

Video in the chain: the best link state of a video tied to each test, recomputed from pm's video index (video/data/video_links.csv), in the counts view; the video rows are the BASS-II main-view recordings (investigation PSI-25, view 'main'; files, bytes, transcribed) for flow_cms only, never for oxygen, pressure, CO, CO2, the CO to CO2 ratio, particle size or aging time; fixtures: ISS P1, oxygen inside and pressure not in the table, 55 counted: 42 / 4 / 0 / 9, main view 49 files, 3,515,643,202 bytes, 7 transcribed; lunar habitat inside 26, 8 with two agreeing labels (all CFI-G), 0 of 17 counted.
